name: Naga Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoot
subtitle: Smoked pork simmered with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha

image.alt: Naga smoked pork with bamboo shoot

ingredients.note: raja mircha traditionally, use far less

prepNotes: Naga cooking uses very little oil and few spices; the flavour is carried by smoke, fermentation and heat. Adding garam masala here would be a mistake.
Fermented bamboo shoot is pungent. Rinse it, and add it in stages, tasting as you go.

steps.text: Rinse the fermented bamboo shoot in two changes of water and drain.
Put the smoked pork in a pot with the ginger, garlic, chillies and just enough water to cover. Bring to a boil.
steps.tip: No oil. The pork renders plenty of its own.

steps.text: Simmer covered 45-60 minutes until the pork is tender and the water has reduced by half.
Add the bamboo shoot and the onion and tomato if using, and cook a further 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Taste before adding all the bamboo. Its sourness varies enormously between batches.

steps.text: Season with salt only at the end; smoked pork is already salty.
Serve with plain rice and a raw chilli on the side.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves. Freezes 2 months.
